blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Sustainable performance, at senior level in the UK, means achieving a steady, high standard of work over many years rather than an extraordinary one for a few quarters. The British business system — patient capital, long partnerships, slowly built reputations — rewards leaders and teams that can deliver consistently. It rarely rewards, and sometimes quietly punishes, the ones who burn themselves out reaching for a single remarkable result.

Boundaries are central to this. It is essential that senior leaders protect their own rest, their own family time, and their own thinking space, because the organisation is watching what they do more than what they say. A leader who works every weekend quietly tells the whole team that weekend work is expected — and the best people, the ones with options, gradually start to leave.

It is critical, therefore, to model the balance you want the team to live. Work hard during the week. Protect the weekend. Take real holidays. Answer fewer evening emails than feels natural. The counter-intuitive result is that, over years, this rhythm produces more output and more loyalty than the opposite approach — and it builds careers that last.

items.q: How does the text define sustainable performance at senior level?
options: The maximum output a leader can produce in a crisis
A steady, high standard maintained over many years
An extraordinary result achieved over a few quarters
Working longer hours than the rest of the team
items.why: "a steady, high standard of work over many years rather than an extraordinary one for a few quarters."

items.q: Why does the author say the organisation watches what leaders DO more than what they say?
options: Because leaders rarely explain their decisions
Because verbal instructions are usually ignored
Because a leader's behaviour sets the team's real expectations
Because British firms distrust formal communication
items.why: "A leader who works every weekend quietly tells the whole team that weekend work is expected" — o comportamento define a norma.

items.q: According to the text, what happens to the best people when a leader never rests?
options: They demand higher pay
They are promoted faster
They work harder to match the leader
They gradually start to leave
items.why: "the best people, the ones with options, gradually start to leave."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: British capital rewards consistency over short bursts
A leader's example shapes the team's habits
Protecting recovery time strengthens long-term output
Burning out for one remarkable quarter is a sound strategy
items.why: Inferência: o texto inteiro argumenta contra sacrificar-se por um único resultado; o sistema britânico até "pune silenciosamente" isso.

items.q: The phrase "the ones with options" most strongly suggests that…
options: these employees are indecisive about their careers
they prefer variety in their tasks
these employees can easily move to another employer
the company offers them flexible working options
items.why: Inferência: "options" aqui = ter para onde ir; são os talentos mais empregáveis, os primeiros a sair de uma cultura de esgotamento.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily orientando uma jovem diretora-executiva. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Can I be honest with you? Eighty hours a week will not make them respect you. It will make them worry about you — and, within a year, it will make some of your best people quietly update their CVs.

I have watched this happen twice. Both directors were brilliant, both convinced that visible exhaustion was the price of the seat. And in both cases the board did not see dedication. They saw a person they could not promote, because there was nowhere left to grow without breaking her.

Here in the UK, the money is patient. Nobody expects you to reinvent the business by Friday. What they are quietly watching is whether you can hold a high standard for five years, not five months. So model the thing you actually want. Protect your weekend. Take the full holiday. Answer the evening emails tomorrow morning — most of them will keep.

It feels counter-intuitive, I know. But the diaries of the executives who last are almost boring. That is the point. Steady beats spectacular, every single time.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: According to Emily, what will an eighty-hour week actually produce?
options: Faster promotion and more respect
Worry from the team and best people looking elsewhere
A reputation for exceptional dedication
A stronger relationship with the board
items.why: "It will make them worry about you — and… make some of your best people quietly update their CVs."

items.q: Why does Emily say the board could not promote the two directors she watched?
options: They had already left the company
Their results were too weak
There was nowhere to grow without breaking them
They refused every new role offered
items.why: "there was nowhere left to grow without breaking her."

items.q: What does Emily mean when she says "the money is patient" in the UK?
options: Backers value a high standard held over years, not weeks
The company is short of capital
Salaries are paid slowly at senior level
Investors expect immediate quarterly returns
items.why: "whether you can hold a high standard for five years, not five months" — capital paciente premia consistência, não pressa.

items.q: Why does Emily say the diaries of the executives who last are "almost boring"?
options: Because they rarely attend important meetings
Because they have very little to do
Because they delegate all of their work
Because a steady, protected rhythm looks unremarkable but endures
items.why: Inferência: "boring" aqui é elogio — a rotina protegida e regular é o que sustenta a carreira; "steady beats spectacular".

items.q: How would you best describe Emily's approach in this coaching conversation?
options: Neutral and purely procedural
Candid and reassuring, redirecting the ambition toward a sustainable pace
Anxious and discouraging about her future
Dismissive of the director's ambition
items.why: Inferência: ela é direta ("Can I be honest?") mas encorajadora, redirecionando a ambição para um ritmo que dura.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We are backed by patient capital, so the board is comfortable with a three-year horizon." Patient capital refers to…
options: capital borrowed at a low interest rate
money set aside for emergencies
funding that demands rapid, short-term returns
investment willing to wait years for a steady return
items.why: Patient capital = capital paciente: investimento que aceita esperar anos por um retorno consistente.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Two of our strongest managers ___ last quarter and are now on extended leave."
options: burned out
signed off
checked in
scaled up
items.why: To burn out = esgotar-se; os gestores se exauriram e tiraram licença.

items.q: "Protecting your own thinking space is not a luxury for a director." Thinking space means…
options: a private office with a door
a quiet meeting room booked in advance
uninterrupted time to reflect and reason
a budget for training courses
items.why: Thinking space = espaço para pensar: tempo protegido para refletir, não um lugar físico.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A leader who rests visibly gives the team permission to set the same ___."
options: boundary
agenda
deadline
target
items.why: Boundary = limite: o exemplo do líder autoriza a equipe a proteger os próprios limites.

items.q: "The result is counter-intuitive: fewer hours produced more output." Counter-intuitive means…
options: obvious to everyone from the start
the opposite of what one would instinctively expect
based only on personal opinion
impossible to measure accurately
items.why: Counter-intuitive = contra-intuitivo: contraria o que o instinto esperaria.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em conversas sobre desempenho e ritmo de trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "I keep telling myself to ease off at weekends, but I never quite manage it." To ease off means to…
options: hide one's workload
work with less intensity
resign from the role
take on extra projects
items.why: Ease off = aliviar o ritmo, reduzir a intensidade.

items.q: "If we don't change the culture, we'll run our best people into the ground." This means we will…
options: exhaust them until they cannot continue
underpay them consistently
relocate them to another office
promote them too quickly
items.why: Run someone into the ground = esgotar alguém completamente, até não aguentar mais.

items.q: "The board wants to see whether the new MD can go the distance." To go the distance means to…
options: sustain performance over the long term
deliver one impressive result
travel frequently for the role
outperform every rival
items.why: Go the distance = aguentar até o fim, manter o desempenho no longo prazo.

items.q: "Let's draw a line at 7pm — no more emails after that." To draw a line means to…
options: make an exception just this once
set a firm limit
delegate the decision upwards
postpone the matter indefinitely
items.why: Draw a line (at) = estabelecer um limite firme, um ponto que não se ultrapassa.

items.q: "A crash-and-sprint culture rarely pays off over a full career." To pay off means to…
options: settle a debt in full
become more expensive
require additional funding
produce a worthwhile result
items.why: Pay off = valer a pena, dar o resultado esperado — aqui, no longo prazo, geralmente não vale.
